description: "Abandoned but not Forgotten" reframes NASA's discarded Moon and Mars equipment as silent monuments of human triumph. Through compelling digital storytelling, we map these mechanical pioneers and narrate the historic missions that left them behind.
summary:
"AstroTales" is a story telling website which is support the children who has the curiosity about what NASA has left behind the Moon, Mars and elsewhere. This web site has been created for 5-18 age children. The mission description layouts has been created considering about the age category to explore the abandoned equipment as they wish. This website provides the children to quizzes and interesting space stories as well.
So, the parents can monitor their children progress through the website.
details:
What it does and how it works

AstroTales is a kid-friendly storytelling website that teaches young explorers, called AstroPals, about the human-made objects left behind on the Moon and Mars. Commander Leo, an animated 3D astronaut with a jetpack, guides them through the journey. Players start with a story intro for the Moon or Mars. They then use a drone-radar map to find 6 Apollo landing sites and 10 Mars landers and rovers (Viking, Pathfinder, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, Perseverance and others). Next they inspect the relics left at each site, with voice narration and real NASA photos, and finally they unlock badges. Trivia quizzes, a Cosmic Lessons section and a Hall of Fame leaderboard keep them coming back.

Benefits

  • It makes space history and “space archaeology” approachable for children through play instead of textbooks.
  • Progress, scores and badges are saved per explorer.
  • Parent and teacher portals let families and classrooms follow along.
  • Admin tools let educators manage lessons, quizzes and announcements.

Intended impact

We want to spark curiosity about space exploration. We also want to teach the next generation that these sites are shared heritage, which means learning about planetary protection and why they should be preserved.

Tools and technology

  • Front end: HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
  • 3D and audio: Three.js for Commander Leo and the planet scene, the Web Audio API for sound effects, and browser speech synthesis for narration.
  • Back end: PHP 8.3 REST endpoints (login, quizzes, lessons, leaderboard, contact, reports).
  • Database: MySQL with 13 tables, including users, quiz scores, badges and lessons.
  • Hosting and content: Laragon (Apache and MySQL) for local development, and photos and mission data from NASA.

Creativity

Instead of a dry data viewer, we wrapped real NASA mission history in a storybook adventure. It has a friendly astronaut character with zero-gravity physics, a drone-radar scanning mechanic, tactile story cards and collectible badges. Mission stories include the “Brave Eagle Lander” (Apollo 11), “Oppy’s 45 km Marathon” and “The Duct-Tape Moon Buggy” (Apollo 17).

Factors we considered

  • Audience: age-appropriate content and language, with voice narration for younger readers.
  • Safety and family involvement: separate roles for child, parent, teacher, admin and super admin.
  • Accuracy: content based on real NASA missions and imagery.
  • Engagement: quizzes, badges and a leaderboard.
  • Accessibility: a simple interface that works in the browser with nothing to install.
